# Assessment — #511: PWA mode: installable client from two origins — localhost (zero TLS) + official hosted URL

_Codebase assessment against 0.13.0-beta.3 (2026-07-12). Effort: **L**._

## Current state (already merged)

Roughly 60-70% of the re-scoped issue is already merged. DONE: (1) `@vite-pwa/sveltekit` is fully wired in packages/client — /home/user/openpalm/packages/client/vite.config.ts exports `pwaOptions` (generateSW, manifest name/short_name/display:standalone/start_url, 192/512 + maskable-512 icons which exist in packages/client/static/, Workbox app-shell precache, NetworkFirst runtime-config.json rule, and rules that never cache credentialed/SSE/no-store responses), verified by packages/client/tests/pwa-config.test.ts (source config + built manifest/sw.js assertions); kit.csp is set in packages/client/svelte.config.js and fonts are self-hosted for offline (static/fonts/). (2) Localhost install origin: stable loopback port 3890 (`DEFAULT_CLIENT_PORT` in packages/lib, re-exported at packages/cli/src/lib/ports.ts:13); zero-dependency static server packages/client/bin/serve.mjs defaults to 3890 (packages/client/tests/serve.test.ts:180-186); `openpalm app` CLI command exists (packages/cli/src/commands/app.ts, opens http://127.0.0.1:3890/chat, tested in app.test.ts) plus `openpalm client-serve` (packages/cli/src/commands/client-serve.ts); Electron spawns the client server on the same port and clears stale SW registrations on build swap (packages/electron/src/main.ts:670-690, 152-166). (3) Offline: IndexedDB connection store with locked-entry seeding from runtime-config.json (packages/client/src/lib/connections/index.ts), `loadRuntimeConfig` never throws (index.ts:424-440), encrypted secret store (src/lib/connections/secrets.ts); extensive bun tests (connections-*.test.ts, boot.test.ts). (4) Guardian CORS allowlist mechanism: `GUARDIAN_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` parsing/enforcement in packages/guardian/src/config.ts:30-63, enforced on direct ingress, integration-tested end-to-end in packages/guardian/src/cors.test.ts (test origin is literally https://app.openpalm.dev); compose default allowlist covers loopback client origins only (packages/skeleton/system/stack/portals.compose.yml:125). (5) Server side of the handshake: GET /api/runtime returns ServerRuntimeContext with contract `version: 2` (packages/ui/src/routes/api/runtime/+server.ts, packages/ui/src/lib/types.ts:36-37). (6) `standalone-pwa` display-mode detection via matchMedia exists in the HOST app only (packages/ui/src/lib/client-context.ts:9-14) — not in the packages/client artifact. (7) Release: `@openpalm/client` npm publish job in .github/workflows/release.yml (npm-client, line 480-488); CI builds the client and runs the purity gate (.github/workflows/ci.yml:256-262). The plan doc itself (docs/technical/ui-runtime-modes-plan.md §12.7 'True remainder', refreshed 2026-07-11) confirms what is still open: hosted-origin CI deploy, client-side /api/runtime handshake, pairing/QR, and HTTPS-refusal UX (`requiresHttpsForRemoteConnections` computed at packages/ui/src/lib/server/features.ts:130 but has zero consumers).

New workflow or release.yml job that publishes packages/client/build to the host after the npm-client job; must serve runtime-config.json-less root with correct no-cache headers for index.html/sw.js/registerSW.js (mirror bin/serve.mjs cache-control semantics, packages/client/tests/serve.test.ts:150-172).

## Test strategy

packages/client unit tests are bun:test files under packages/client/tests/*.test.ts, run via `bun run client:test` at the repo root or `cd packages/client && bun test`; note pwa-config.test.ts and the purity gate require `bun run client:build` first (root package.json _test:note). Write new handshake/refusal/display-mode tests there first (existing helpers: tests/helpers/mocks.ts, fake-idb.ts, contract.ts). Playwright e2e lives in packages/client/e2e/*.pw.ts, run with `cd packages/client && bun run test:e2e` (playwright.config.ts starts its own webServer; `bun run test:browsers` installs chromium) — add the offline-shell test here using context.setOffline. Guardian CORS-default changes are covered by `bun test packages/guardian/` (cors.test.ts spawns a real guardian process with GUARDIAN_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS). Host-side pairing endpoints in packages/ui use vitest *.vitest.ts files, run with `cd packages/ui && npm run test:unit -- --run` (browser-project *.svelte.vitest.ts cannot run in the dev container — proxy-blocked Playwright download, per plan §12.6). CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) already builds the client and runs the aggregate `bun run test`, so new bun tests execute automatically.

## Dependencies (0.13.0 open issues)

- #557 — Guardian edge TLS + CORS (Phase 6.5): hard prerequisite for the phone/hosted half (mixed-content rule means every hosted-client -> guardian connection needs TLS); also owns baking the official origin into the CORS default and shares the requiresHttpsForRemoteConnections client-side refusal criterion.
- #435 — Guardian auth: the pairing flow (QR/one-time code) must mint guardian principal credentials rather than a parallel mechanism; Basic direct-principal auth is already live in packages/guardian (cors.test.ts seeds principals) but the pairing coordination point is this issue.
- #486 — Remote-only client install / connection management: the pairing UX lands on top of the /connections management surface (client side already extracted to packages/client/src/routes/connections/); host-side mint UI belongs to the #486 surface in packages/ui.

## Risks

- Hosting provider for app.openpalm.dev is TBD in the plan — the CI-deploy work item is blocked on an infra decision outside the repo.
- Service-worker precache pinning: an installed PWA at the hosted origin keeps the old build until sw.js changes; deploy pipeline must preserve the no-cache semantics bin/serve.mjs enforces locally (index.html/sw.js/registerSW.js) or installs wedge (the H2/H3 review findings in serve.test.ts and Electron clearClientOrigin exist precisely because this bit them on localhost).
- Phone acceptance criterion is untestable end-to-end until #557 lands (no TLS anywhere in the stack today) — the issue can only close its hosted-path criteria against a TLS-fronted guardian.
- The /api/runtime handshake endpoint lives in packages/ui (adapter-node host), but many client connections are plain OpenCode or guardian direct-ingress base URLs that have no /api/runtime — handshake logic must treat 404 as 'older/plain instance', not an error.
- Pairing introduces a new credential-issuance surface (one-time codes) — needs the same review rigor as #435; secrets must land in the client's encrypted secret store (secretRef), never in the QR-visible connection record.
- Guardian CORS default-origin change touches portals.compose.yml which ships to every install — a wrong default silently opens the hosted origin to LAN guardians that never opted in (mitigated by GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS defaulting off).

## Original issue body

# #511: PWA mode: installable client from two origins — localhost (zero TLS) + official hosted URL

## Re-scoped 2026-07-06 (ratified — see `docs/technical/ui-client-split-assessment.md`)

The PWA is the new **`@openpalm/client`** static app (`adapter-static` + `@vite-pwa/sveltekit`), not the adapter-node host build. Host features are **absent from the artifact**, not capability-hidden. Revised design: `docs/technical/ui-runtime-modes-plan.md` §6.10, Phase 6.

### Two primary install origins (simplicity guardrail: TLS is never a manual user task on default paths)

1. **Localhost (desktop, zero setup).** The harness/CLI serves the built client on a **stable loopback port** (PWA identity = origin incl. port). `http://127.0.0.1` is a secure context → installable with no certificates. A loopback origin is exempt from mixed-content blocking and sits in the most-trusted Private Network Access tier, so it can talk to plain-HTTP LAN guardians. Entry points: Electron menu / host-app button ("Install OpenPalm app") and `openpalm app`.
2. **Official hosted URL** (e.g. `https://app.openpalm.dev`). CI publishes the same static build to a canonical TLS-terminated origin — one install for any phone/tablet, connecting to any of the user's instances.

### Platform constraints this design is built around (why the original "same build" scope changed)

- **Secure context:** a PWA is only installable over HTTPS or from `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`. A UI served over plain HTTP on a LAN IP is *never* installable — the original plan had no answer for mobile install.
- **Mixed content:** an HTTPS origin cannot `fetch()` plain-HTTP guardians → the hosted path requires guardian TLS (tracked in the Phase 6.5 workstream issue; Tailscale `ts.net` certs recommended default). Any phone → guardian connection effectively requires TLS.
- **Per-origin identity:** one installed PWA = one origin; multi-instance switching must be in-app (the `/connections` switcher + IndexedDB store), which also means one hosted origin can serve *all* of a user's instances.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `@vite-pwa/sveltekit` in `packages/client`: manifest, icons (192/512 + maskable), Workbox app-shell precache
- [ ] Desktop: install prompt from `http://127.0.0.1:<stable port>` with zero TLS setup
- [ ] Phone: install from the official hosted URL
- [ ] Add/switch connections via paste-or-scan pairing (host app mints QR / one-time code — plan §6.6)
- [ ] Hosted client refuses plain-HTTP non-loopback targets with an actionable message (deep-link to the TLS guide)
- [ ] `/api/runtime` contract-version handshake: hosted client degrades gracefully against older instances
- [ ] Guardian CORS allowlist includes the official origin (coordinates with Phase 6.5 issue)
- [ ] Offline: app shell + saved connections (IndexedDB) render offline; no blank page; service worker never caches credentialed responses
- [ ] When installed, `clientDisplayMode` resolves to `standalone-pwa` via `matchMedia`

### Dependencies

- Phase 5 — `packages/client` + `packages/ui-kit` extraction (tracked separately)
- Phase 6.5 — guardian edge TLS + CORS (gates the phone story; tracked separately)
- #509 — RuntimeContext (Phase 1)
- #486 — connection management (Phase 2)
- #435 — Guardian auth (credentials for remote connections)

<summary>Original scope (2026-06-20) — superseded by the re-scope above</summary>

## Summary

Make the OpenPalm UI installable as a PWA on mobile and desktop. The PWA is the **same SvelteKit build** (adapter-node + service worker) — no new UI, no duplicate pages. Capabilities hide host controls when there is no local stack.

## Background

The PWA install path enables a phone or tablet to install OpenPalm as an app that connects to a remote assistant (either an `assistant-container` instance or a full stack behind Guardian). This is the completion of #486 (remote-only install) on mobile.

## Design

Full design in `docs/technical/ui-runtime-modes-plan.md` §6.10 and Phase 6.

### What makes it a PWA

Two additions to the existing build:

1. `packages/ui/static/manifest.webmanifest` — name, icons, `display: standalone`, `start_url: /`
2. `packages/ui/src/service-worker.ts` — SvelteKit auto-registers; precaches app shell + static assets

No new pages. No separate build. No duplicate UI code.

### How features are hidden

When `hostMode === 'pwa-static'`, `resolveCapabilities()` returns only:
- `connections:manage`, `connections:switch`, `chat`, `pwa:install`

All components check `hasCapability(cap)`. Host-only nav items are absent because `hasCapability('host:stack:read')` is false — not because of branching UI code or separate routes.

### Effective capability matrix for PWA

| Active connection | Available |
|---|---|
| None | `/connections/new` (landing), `pwa:install` |
| Remote assistant | `chat`, `connections:switch`, `connections:manage` |
| Remote assistant-container (future, via `grantedCapabilities`) | + `assistant-settings:read/write` |

### Offline support

IndexedDB connection store: connection records are readable offline (cached), writes queued and replayed when reconnected.

### Auth

Remote connections use Guardian Basic auth, coordinated with #435 Bearer static token seam.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `static/manifest.webmanifest` present; browser shows install prompt on supported platforms
- [ ] Service worker precaches app shell; offline shows shell (not blank page)
- [ ] When installed as PWA, `clientDisplayMode` resolves to `standalone-pwa` via `matchMedia`
- [ ] `hasCapability('host:stack:read')` returns false in PWA mode — host tabs not visible and not reachable
- [ ] `/api/host/*` returns 403 even if a PWA client sends a direct request (server-enforced, not just hidden)
- [ ] PWA can add a remote assistant connection (`/connections/new`) and open chat
- [ ] PWA can switch between saved connections
- [ ] Connection records readable offline (IndexedDB); no blank/crash on loss of connectivity
- [ ] Icons provided at minimum 192×192 and 512×512 for install prompt

## Dependencies

- #509 — RuntimeContext (capability resolution, `pwa-static` host mode) — Phase 1
- #486 — Connection management at `/connections` — Phase 2
- Capability-driven landing (Phase 3) — PWA landing at `/connections/new` when no connection configured
